questions.stem: Which Resource Profile can be used to define when start and stop a resource?
questions.explanation: Schedule Profile defines when to start and stop a resource (D). It specifies time-based availability windows for cloud resources. Security Profile (A) manages security group assignments. Application Profile (B) handles post-provision app configuration. Lease Profile (C) defines duration-based lifecycle controls, not start/stop schedules.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for a Compute Profile? (Choose two.)

options.text: Defines what virtual hardware is presented to end users
Defines custom t-shirt sizes (small, medium, large, etc.) for virtual hardware
Defines OS choices for Cloud Catalog offerings
Defines when virtual hardware can be provisioned by end users

questions.explanation: Compute Profile defines custom t-shirt sizes (B) such as small/medium/large for virtual hardware, and defines when virtual hardware can be provisioned (E). It does not define virtual hardware presented to end users (A — that is Catalog Item), OS choices (C — OS Profile), or Security Groups (D — Security Profile).

questions.stem: Which Permission would you use to make a Catalog Item for a cloud native application that you plan to release, viewable but not executable, for users who belong to the Marketing Developers group?
questions.explanation: The Viewer permission makes a Catalog Item visible but not executable (C). Users with Viewer can browse and inspect the item without running it. Execute (D) allows provisioning. Access (B) provides broader access. All (A) grants all permissions. Viewer satisfies the 'viewable but not executable' requirement for Marketing Developers.

questions.stem: What governance objects are available in Cloud Provisioning and Governance? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Governance objects in CPG are Quotas (A), Policies (C), and Permissions (D). Quotas limit resource consumption, Policies enforce compliance rules, Permissions control who can provision what. Credentials (B) are configuration objects for cloud provider authentication. SLAs (E) are service management objects not part of CPG governance.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes what Puppet, Chef, Ansible Tower and Salt are utilized for?
questions.explanation: Puppet, Chef, Ansible Tower, and Salt are configuration management tools (B). They automate software configuration and enforce desired state on servers. They are not cost control (A), cloud monitoring (C), or continuous integration platforms (D).

questions.stem: Cloud Scripts and Cloud Script Templates utilize which host based scripting tools to install software?
questions.explanation: Cloud Scripts and Cloud Script Templates use shell scripts (Linux) and PowerShell scripts (Windows) for host-based software installation (A). Python/Ruby (B) and JavaScript/Perl (C/D) are not the host-based scripting tools used by CPG for software installation on provisioned VMs.

questions.stem: How are variables grouped for a Catalog Item?
What must be created in Azure before you can configure Azure Alerts in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: A Resource Group must be created in Azure before configuring Azure Alerts in ServiceNow (B). All Azure resources, including alert configurations, belong to a Resource Group. A Network Security Group (A) controls traffic. An App Service (C) hosts web apps. A Monitor Alert (D) is created after the Resource Group exists.

questions.stem: What application can you use in the Cloud Admin Portal to guide your organization through the process of setting up Cloud Provisioning and Governance?
questions.explanation: The Guided Setup application (D) in the Cloud Admin Portal walks administrators through the process of configuring Cloud Provisioning and Governance. Guided Setup provides step-by-step wizards for configuring integrations. Cloud Orchestration (A), Configuration Templates (B), and Cloud Planner (C) are not the setup wizard application.

questions.stem: Which Cloud Provider feature do organizations depend on to provide visibility into resource management and billing? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Organizations depend on Billing Data (B) for financial visibility into resource consumption and Tags (D) for cost allocation and resource attribution. Security Groups (A) control access. Identity and Authentication Management (C) handles access control, not billing/resource visibility.

questions.stem: IT has implemented a new poet identification code, and they would like to be able to analyze cloud consumption based upon this code. What features would you use in Cloud Provisioning and Governance to implement this request? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add a new Project Tag to the Tag Definitions
Create a Resource Pool associated to the projects table
Add new parameter to the CAPI interface

questions.explanation: To analyze cloud consumption based on a new project identification code, Create a Cloud Script (C) to process and apply the code and add a new CAPI parameter (D) to the interface to pass the identifier through provisioning workflows. Adding a Tag Definition (A) helps labeling but is insufficient alone. A Resource Pool (B) is for grouping, not analysis.

questions.stem: The Manager of the Marketing team wants to have control over the Cloud Resources provisioned through Cloud Provisioning and Governance. What feature in Cloud Provisioning and Governance should you use to satisfy this request?
questions.explanation: Governance Rules (B) give managers control over cloud resources provisioned through CPG. Governance Rules enforce policies on what resources teams can deploy, enforcing compliance. Management Request (A) and Approval Policy (D) handle individual requests. Policy Action Script (C) is for scripted policy enforcement, not manager-level governance control.

questions.stem: What mechanism can be used by Cloud Provisioning and Governance to abstract vendor-specific cloud resources from end users?
questions.explanation: Templates (C) abstract vendor-specific cloud resources from end users by providing a standardized interface (CFT for AWS, ARM for Azure) that hides provider-specific details. Policies (A) enforce compliance. Workflows (B) orchestrate provisioning steps. Resource Profiles (D) define resource options but don't abstract vendor specifics.

questions.stem: What AWS services must be configured for Cloud Provisioning and Governance to receive alerts from AWS? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS SNS Topic (B) receives and routes alert notifications to ServiceNow endpoints, and AWS Config (D) triggers configuration change alerts. AWS CloudTrail (A) provides audit logging, not alerts. AWS Control Tower (C) manages multi-account governance. AWS CloudWatch (E) generates metrics but SNS/Config are the integration points.

questions.stem: Which object is rendered as a tab on the request form of a Cloud Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: Variable Sets (D) are rendered as tabs on the request form of a Cloud Catalog Item, organizing related variables into logical groups. Tab Set (A) and Tab Group (B) are not standard ServiceNow Catalog concepts. Variable Group (C) is used within forms but not rendered as a tab at the catalog item level.

questions.stem: For Cloud Provisioning and Governance in the Orlando release or later, where can you utilize an Application Profile?
questions.explanation: In the Orlando release or later, Application Profiles can be utilized in post-provision operations (D) to configure applications after VM provisioning completes. Server side includes (A) and MID Server script includes (B) are not CPG profile contexts. Blueprints stage operations (C) were the pre-Orlando approach.

questions.stem: What would you review to quickly determine which group is deploying the most stacks?
questions.explanation: The Cloud Operations Dashboard (A) provides at-a-glance metrics on deployment activity, including which groups are deploying the most stacks. Cloud Activities (B) shows event logs. Cloud Request Items (C) shows individual requests. Cloud Orchestration Trail (D) shows workflow execution history, not group deployment summaries.

questions.stem: What feature of CPG supports the use of Quotas for Templates?
When designing an ARM or CFT backed Catalog Item, how can you ensure that the Order Form variable automatically presents with a list of appropriate CIs from the ServiceNow CMDB?
questions.explanation: Expressions (A) are used to ensure Order Form variables automatically present appropriate CMDB CIs for ARM/CFT-backed Catalog Items. Expressions dynamically query the CMDB based on conditions to populate variable choice lists. Mappings (B) link template variables to catalog inputs. Conditions (C) control visibility. Metadata (D) provides template information.

questions.stem: After ingesting a new version of a Template, what can be done to ensure that the Order Form reflects the changes that were introduced in the new version of the Template?

options.text: Modify the Catalog Item’s Cloud Variables
Deactivate and activate the Catalog Item

questions.stem: What feature or product capability must be utilized to gather credentials for a post provisioning operation?

A customer on the New York release of CPG currently uses Blueprints to deploy Azure VMs. What deployment options are available to the customer when they upgrade to the latest release of CPG? (Choose two.)

options.text: Customers cannot upgrade from New York

questions.explanation: When upgrading from the New York release, Jenkins Workflow (A) and Puppet Manifest (C) are available deployment options in the latest CPG release. Azure ARM Templates (D) are a separate deployment method. The Azure Blueprint Service (B) is Azure-native and not a CPG option. Customers can upgrade from New York (E is incorrect).

questions.stem: How can the required parameters for a CAPI Operation be determined?

options.text: The Cloud Provider documentation and testing
Reference the parameters used by another CAPI Operation

questions.explanation: Required parameters for a CAPI Operation are determined from ServiceNow product documentation (D) for each cloud provider integration. The ServiceNow docs specify required and optional parameters for each CAPI Operation. Cloud Provider documentation (A) describes the underlying API. ECMA script docs (C) are for JavaScript. Referencing other operations (B) is not the defined method.

questions.stem: When creating a new CAPI API, what is the suggested starting version number to prevent conflicts with out-of-the-box CAPI APIs?
What type of script is required for executing code to make a REST API call for a CAPI Operation?
Which JavaScript Class can be used to make a REST API call to AWS with the least amount of code?
What CI Class Type attribute is required by Cloud Provisioning and Governance to determine uniqueness?
questions.explanation: The sys_id attribute is required by Cloud Provisioning and Governance to determine CI uniqueness (A). sys_id is ServiceNow's universal unique identifier for every record, including CIs, making it the definitive uniqueness attribute. name (B) can be non-unique. object_id (C) and correlation_id (D) are supplementary identifiers, not the primary uniqueness determinant.

questions.stem: What Resource Block component is used to organize the Methods required to perform an Operation?
questions.explanation: Bindings (C) organize the Methods required to perform an Operation within a Resource Block. Bindings link method calls to their associated operations, defining how each operation invokes the underlying API methods. Method blocks (A) define individual methods. Steps (B) are sequential workflow units. Endpoint operations (D) define the API endpoints.

questions.stem: Which three CAPI components must be configured to create a CAPI Extension?

options.text: CAPI Vendor, CAPI Interface, and CAPI REST API
CAPI Product, CAPI Method, and CAPI API
CAPI Vendor, CAPI Interface, and CAPI API
CAPI Provider, CAPI Interface, and CAPI API

questions.explanation: Three components required to create a CAPI Extension are CAPI Vendor (defines the cloud provider), CAPI Interface (defines available operations), and CAPI REST API (defines the REST API spec) (A). CAPI Product/Method/API (B) uses incorrect terms. CAPI Provider (C/D) is a configured instance, not a component required for extension creation.

questions.stem: When testing a REST API, you receive status code of 200 from the Cloud Service. What does this mean?

options.text: A value of 200 is not a valid code
The call resulted in a server error
The call resulted in a client error

questions.explanation: HTTP status code 200 means the call was successful (A). 200 OK is the standard success response for REST API calls. It is a valid and universally recognized code (B is incorrect). Server errors are 5xx codes (500, 503). Client errors are 4xx codes (400, 404). Any CPG REST integration receiving 200 indicates the cloud service processed the request successfully.

questions.stem: When authoring a new CAPI Extension, what must you create to define the operations that will be available for the new cloud service?
questions.explanation: When authoring a new CAPI Extension, create a CAPI Interface (C) to define the operations available for the new cloud service. The Interface is the contract/spec describing what operations can be performed. CAPI Provider (A) is a configured instance implementing an interface. CAPI API (B) defines the underlying REST calls. CAPI Product (D) represents the cloud service offering.

questions.stem: Before you can author a new Resource Block, what information do you require about the Host Resource Block that the Resource Block you are authoring will connect to?
Which of the following is NOT a supported expression type in a Resource Block?
Which CAPI components must be configured for a Day-2 CAPI Operation? (Choose two.)
When using a CFT or an ARM Template what feature of Cloud Provisioning and Governance is used to deploy software?
questions.explanation: When using a CFT or ARM Template, OS Profiles (A) are used to define and deploy software configurations for provisioned resources. Cloud Scripts (B) install software on running VMs post-provision. Compute Profile (C) defines virtual hardware sizing. Blueprints (D) were the legacy approach replaced by CFT/ARM Templates.

questions.stem: When a custom workflow is called by a resource block operation, what activity should be used to get information about the operation from the Cloud Provisioning and Governance application?
What API does Cloud Provisioning and Governance utilize to add and update entries in the CMDB?
questions.explanation: Cloud Provisioning and Governance uses the Identification Reconciliation Engine (IRE) (A) to add and update entries in the CMDB. The IRE is ServiceNow's standard CMDB API for CI identification, deduplication, and reconciliation. CMDBTransformUtil (B) handles data transformations. CMDBGroupAPI (C) is not a standard ServiceNow CMDB API. CI Reconciliation API (D) is a subset function of the IRE.

questions.stem: Which role should be utilized for cloud alerts?
questions.explanation: The Cloud Administrator role (sn_cmp.cmp_root_admin) (C) should be utilized for cloud alerts, providing complete access to configure and receive cloud monitoring alerts. Cloud Governor (A) manages governance rules. Cloud Operator (B) manages day-to-day operations. Cloud event integration (D) is a specific role for event processing integrations.

questions.stem: What are the three available Tag Types in Tag Management?
questions.explanation: The three available Tag Types in CPG Tag Management are Internal, External, and ServiceNow (A). Internal tags are used within the organization, External tags are cloud provider-specific tags, and ServiceNow tags are platform-managed. AWS/Azure/ServiceNow (B) are providers, not tag types. Custom Tags (C) and User-defined (D) are not the standard type names.

questions.stem: In AWS, the region-specific containers for virtual resources are called regions. In Cloud Provisioning and Governance, regions are called what?
When working with Azure any service that is used must be associated with a _______________?
questions.explanation: In Azure, any service used must be associated with a Subscription (A). Azure Subscriptions are the fundamental billing and management scope that all Azure resources belong to. Diagnostic Logs (B) are monitoring features. Storage Account (C) is a specific service. Tags (D) are organizational labels. Availability Sets (E) are for VM high-availability grouping only.

questions.stem: The Azure Resource Manager uses what to organize the cloud resources required to deploy a VM?
questions.explanation: Azure Resource Manager uses Resource Groups (D) to organize the cloud resources required to deploy a VM. Resource Groups are the fundamental ARM organizational unit containing all related resources (VMs, NICs, disks, etc.) for a deployment. Resource Pool (A) is a VMware/ServiceNow concept. Storage Account (B) stores data. Placement Group (C) is for proximity placement.

questions.stem: Which Service in AWS is used to send alert messages to Cloud Provisioning and Governance?
What objet does a Catalog Item utilize to dynamically set values for a Resource Block attribute?
questions.explanation: Catalog Items use Expressions (B) to dynamically set values for Resource Block attributes. Expressions evaluate conditions and compute values based on order form input, CMDB data, or other variables. Methods (A) define API call implementations. Functions (C) are not a CPG Catalog concept. Operations (D) define what actions are performed, not dynamic attribute values.

questions.stem: When deploying an IIS Web Server in AWS for public access, which of the following must be configured to allow users to access the Web Server?

options.text: Security Group that allows inbound traffic
Network Traffic Group that allows inbound traffic

questions.explanation: When deploying an IIS Web Server in AWS for public access, a Security Group allowing inbound traffic (B) must be configured to allow HTTP/HTTPS access (ports 80/443). AWS Security Groups act as virtual firewalls. A TLS Certificate (A) enables HTTPS but is not required for basic access. Network Traffic Group (C) is not an AWS concept. Windows Host Based Firewall (D) would block traffic by default.
